definitions.explanation: The length of time a person or organism lives, or the expected duration of life.
The expected duration of functionality for machines, products, or other non-living things before they wear out or need replacement.

examples.japanese: {日本人|にほんじん}の{平均|へいきん}{寿命|じゅみょう}は{長|なが}い。
examples.english: The average lifespan of Japanese people is long.

examples.japanese: {医学|いがく}の{進歩|しんぽ}で{寿命|じゅみょう}が{延|の}びた。
examples.english: Lifespans have increased due to advances in medicine.

examples.japanese: {健康|けんこう}{寿命|じゅみょう}を{延|の}ばすことが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It is important to extend healthy life expectancy.

examples.japanese: バッテリーの{寿命|じゅみょう}が{短|みじか}い。
この{製品|せいひん}の{寿命|じゅみょう}は{約|やく}{十年|じゅうねん}だ。
examples.english: The service life of this product is about ten years.

examples.japanese: エアコンの{寿命|じゅみょう}が{来|き}たので{買|か}い{替|か}えた。
examples.english: The air conditioner reached the end of its life, so I replaced it.

notes:
USAGE:
{寿命|じゅみょう} is used for both living things and products/machines. When used for products, it functions similarly to English "lifespan" or "service life."

COLLOCATIONS:
- {平均|へいきん}{寿命|じゅみょう} — average lifespan
- {健康|けんこう}{寿命|じゅみょう} — healthy life expectancy
- {寿命|じゅみょう}が{延|の}びる — lifespan increases
- {寿命|じゅみょう}が{縮|ちぢ}む — lifespan shortens
- {寿命|じゅみょう}が{来|く}る — to reach end of life

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan has one of the highest average lifespans in the world. The concept of {健康|けんこう}{寿命|じゅみょう} (healthy life expectancy) — years lived in good health, as opposed to total lifespan — has become an important topic in public health discussions.
